summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted with weakness and acute blood loss anemia due to epistaxis and microscopic hematuria, occurring in the setting of a supratherapeutic INR from warfarin. He received two units of packed red blood cells, with improvement in hemoglobin from 8.6 to 10.7 g/dL. Coumadin and aspirin were held initially and later restarted at a reduced dose. His nose was packed by ENT, and he was started on nasal saline and short-term Afrin to prevent re-bleeding. Hyponatremia improved with volume repletion and temporary discontinuation of Lasix, which was resumed at discharge. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout, with no evidence of active bleeding or intracranial pathology on imaging. He was discharged home with follow-up arranged in primary care, ENT, and urology, and instructions for monitoring weight and bleeding symptoms.
